brief: Three desks describe the same setup. US equities sit just below record highs while positioning and sentiment stay depressed. JPMorgan's Schlegel reports aggregate positioning little changed, modest hedge fund re-grossing of 1.3 sigma, global nets at the 40th to 50th percentile and sentiment turning less constructive. Goldman Prime Brokerage shows US equities slightly net bought at +0.2 standard deviations, single stocks bought against macro product short sales, with long/short gross leverage at 208.5% and net at 48.4%, near Liberation Day lows. Goldman's Privorotsky ties the heaviness in the S&P and mega caps to the FX carry unwind. Bessent claims Treasury visibility into BOJ policy, a BOJ hike looks imminent, the yen appreciates and leverage diffuses out of the system. Nomura's McElligott names a Negative Risk Trinity behind low positioning. September and midterm seasonality, UST supply crowding out duration, and a hawkish central bank impulse off commodity surges. Because the market is short, rallies force chasing, a mystery buyer has spent $315mm of premium on AI-name calls, and VIX 3-month call skew sits at the 91st percentile. Goldman's Flood argues the opposite, that 30% Q2 EPS growth, bearish sentiment gauges and the IPO pipeline make positioning too cautious.
